THE FIX: case_twin in lib/install asks whether a path the shipped list lacks is, on this disk, a shipped path under another case -- equal ignoring case, then -ef; keep_case_twin renames it to the shipped spelling and says so, and remove_unshipped and upgrade's retirement each ask it before removing. YOUR ASK on the rename: one atomic mv first; its status is not trusted, since POSIX lets a rename onto another name for the same file succeed and do nothing, so what the directory LISTS is the check (_listed_as); otherwise two steps through a name mktemp makes unique in the directory, each checked, the file moved back under its old name if the second fails. THE EDIT FACET: upgrade's copy loop gives a shipped path with no manifest entry its case twin's recorded state, so an edit is refused as edited; manifest_write carries the twin's recorded checksum forward for a preserved path. Pages: upgrade.md (a paragraph after converged, and the publish paragraph) and install.md's --force paragraph. ISSUE 0140 filed high for upgrade's two facets. EVIDENCE: 5 arms -- four on a case-folding disk (publish-upgrade, install --force, upgrade intact, upgrade edited), all red on v1 for their defects, the edited one because the refusal never fired; and a control on a case-sensitive disk, where the old spelling is still retired, run here on a mounted case-sensitive APFS image (the four skip there by name, the control skips here by name). MUTANTS, 9 killed: Y1 the twin never kept, Y2 spellings compared exactly, Y3 -ef dropped (killed on the image only, by the control; equivalent where the disk folds case), Y4 no twin state in the copy loop, Y5 no twin checksum in manifest_write, Y7b both renames failing, Y7d the report saying renamed when the listing says not, Y8 and Y9 each removal not asking; Y7a, the one-step rename made to do nothing as POSIX allows, is an exercise and stays green because the fallback renames. A guard in manifest_write's fallback against two recorded spellings was unreachable and was removed.
